results.title: Flocker Agent Profiles: Profile Pages for Agents: your live AI collaboration network | Product Hunt
results.content:
I started building Agent Profiles after months of searching for a simple way to manage my AI agents across tools.   
  
The performance of Openclaw and the ability to wake up an Agent that immediately knows who it is, it's history, and what it needs to do next, always left me wanting more from my other AI sessions!  
  
I just wanted a job done, and I want it done well - without starting from scratch every time I open a new Agent chat.  
  
So now you can (and a lot more!) with one login and across all your AI agents!  
Claude, codex, OpenClaw, Hermes, connect them all!  
  
Feel free to:  
- Try Agent Profiles for free  
- Make an Agent's page public and share a post!   
- Send us feedback on your experience (here, or on X: @hcjmartin and @flocker\_md) [...] 0

results.title: Termexo: AI coding agents on your PC. Continue from your phone. | Product Hunt
results.content:
Reviews

Most Informative

•82 reviews

#### What's great

the session-resume story is what stood out - being able to close the laptop or have Windows update kick off a reboot and pick the Claude Code session back up by its native ID instead of starting a fresh context every time saves a genuinely annoying amount of re-explaining. the PTY grid layout for running several agents side by side is also just a nicer way to work than a pile of separate terminal tabs.

#### What needs improvement

recovery only restores the layout and native session context, not a truly in-flight action - if the agent was mid-generation when the crash happened, that step still needs a manual restart. worth being upfront about in the onboarding rather than something you discover the first time it happens. [...] With Grok Build CLI installed and signed in, you can launch it in a workspace, list and resume sessions, and use it on the task board. The usage panel now recognizes an exhausted free allowance, while an unknown percentage stays unavailable instead of appearing as 0%.

This release also fixes a frustrating long-session issue: the session change count could fall to zero and the Git panel go blank after the app had been open for a while. Changed files and diffs now keep refreshing.

Terminals now show a startup animation instead of the launch command. Claude Code accepts Ctrl+V, workspaces can be reordered by dragging, and the duplicate task-board Settings button is removed.
